# 1on1 Devon - 2026-05-22

**Time:** 30 min, Friday 9 AM
**Format:** Skip-level, every other week ([[Devon Park]] reports to Marcus)

## What Devon brought up

**Stopgap duty is grinding him down.** Since April he's been babysitting the Sidekiq ACH batch: extra workers, a manual check against the 6 PM PT cutoff every weekday, a Sunday-evening eyeball on volume. It works. It's also eating a third of his week, and he's frustrated that it's taking time from the outbox worker.

I told him: the stopgap is the thing keeping us from a second April 6. It matters. But he's right that it shouldn't be him forever. We agreed: two more weeks, then it goes into the on-call rotation with a written checklist so it isn't tribal knowledge.

**Shadow-mode diff harness.** He's building the outbox worker for ADR-024 and wants to write a nightly diff harness before anything touches production: replay the day's ACH intents through the new pipeline in shadow, compare against what Sidekiq actually sent, flag every mismatch. I asked about coverage. He said the harness comes first, before any cut-over talk. That's the right answer.

He'll build it in Go, mirroring Marcus's patterns. Harness can ship on Marcus's async review. Anything that touches production still needs Marcus's eyes.

**Payments is too small.** It came up sideways: how many things he can't get to. I read it as: he wants another payments engineer. Honest answer: yes. We have a strong senior backend candidate in final rounds (Sarah K). If she joins, she lands on Payments, and I'd like Devon to be her onboarding buddy.

**Career growth.** He's getting recruiter outreach from a couple of big-name payments infrastructure companies. He told me up front. Not pressure, transparency.

I asked: are you happy here? Yes, but "I want to feel like I'm growing." What does growth look like? He's clear: he wants to grow into staff. Own a system end to end, not just a component. Write and talk about the work (he'd like to do a talk on the outbox pattern once it's in production). Mentor someone.

My response: all three are possible. Conference travel budget is approved (Aleks signed off). Writing time: 10% of his week. Mentorship: the next payments hire. And the outbox worker is exactly the kind of end-to-end ownership a staff case gets built on.

## What I brought up

**April 6.** He's the one who spotted the anomaly: throughput falling off on his dashboard before the batch fully stalled. I thanked him explicitly. He shrugged it off. Noting it for his review.

**Working with Marcus.** Better since the cutover planning got more structured. Watching for friction as both of them push code into the same pipeline. Fine for now.

**Comp.** I said it out loud: his comp is below market. We fix it at the next review cycle, after the Series B. He wasn't surprised, but I wanted to say it explicitly.

## Commitments

- [x] Devon: two more weeks of stopgap duty, then hand to on-call with a checklist
- [x] Devon: shadow-mode diff harness before any cut-over date is set
- Devon: think about what a good first project for the next payments hire looks like
- [x] Me: conference budget confirmed
- [x] Me: 10% writing time, starting next week
- Me: explicit comp conversation post-Series B

## What I'm not bringing up yet

He's been sketching, in his evenings, a ledger-level reconciliation job: check our books against the bank's and the broker's every night, alert on any drift. Has mentioned it casually. Side project or future system? Fuzzy. I want to engage, but he hasn't pitched it. Let him bring it.

## Read on Devon this week

Most thoughtful 1:1 in months. The recruiter outreach has been a useful prompt for him to say what he wants. Healthy.

## Personal note

Devon is the engineer I'm most worried about losing. Not because he's unhappy. Because he's that good and the market knows it. Conference + writing + mentorship is real but might not be enough. The post-Series B comp adjustment has to land right.
